name: Electromagnetic radiation
credit: Based on the Chapter 1 summary in Cambridge Senior Science Physics VCE Units 1&2. Diagrams drawn for this page.

pts: A **wave** carries **energy**, not matter. Particles vibrate on the spot.
**Mechanical** waves (sound, water) need a **medium**. EM waves do not.
**Transverse**: vibrates at 90° to the direction of travel. e.g. light.
**Longitudinal**: vibrates along the direction of travel. e.g. sound. **Compressions** (close) and **rarefactions** (spread out).

where: **amplitude**: biggest distance from the neutral position (m)

pts: The **medium** sets $v$. The **source** sets $f$. $\lambda$ is the result.
Shake faster: $f$ up, $\lambda$ shorter, $v$ the same.
**EM wave**: vibrating **electric** and **magnetic** fields.
**Transverse**: the fields vibrate at 90° to the direction of travel.
Needs **no medium**, so it crosses a vacuum. Sound cannot.
In a vacuum all EM waves travel at the **speed of light**, $c$.

where: speed of light in a vacuum, $3.00 \times 10^{8}$ m/s. Use Hz and m.

pts: Same $c$, so a shorter $\lambda$ means a higher $f$ and more energy.
**Sunlight**: about half infrared, a bit less than half visible and about 7% ultraviolet.
Long $\lambda$ (radio, microwave): low energy. Used to **communicate**.
Short $\lambda$ (UV, X-ray, gamma): high energy. Can **damage cells**.

1B-strip.note: **The EM spectrum** with approximate boundaries. Left to right: $\lambda$ shorter, $f$ and energy higher. Visible: violet 400 nm to red 700 nm.

pts: A **ray** shows the direction light travels. **Crests** are at 90° to it.
The **normal** is at 90° to the surface. Measure angles from it.
**Reflection**: angle in = angle out.
**Refraction**: light bends because its speed changes.
Slower (bigger $n$): bends **towards** the normal. Faster: **away**.
$f$ stays the same. Slower: shorter $\lambda$, crests closer.

where: **refractive index**: light is $n$ times slower than in a vacuum (no unit)
speed of light in the material (m/s)
angle between the ray and the normal (°)

pts: **Prac**: graph $\sin\theta_1$ (air) up, $\sin\theta_2$ (glass) across. Gradient = $n$ of the glass.
**Images**: the eye traces rays back in straight lines, so things under water look **higher** than they are.
**Dispersion**: white light splits into colours because $n$ depends on the colour. **Prac**: a prism.
Violet: biggest $n$, slowest in glass, bends most. Red bends least.
**Chromatic distortion**: a lens focuses each colour at a different point.
**Partial internal reflection**: part reflects, part refracts.
**Critical angle** $\theta_c$: the angle of incidence where the refracted ray skims along the surface ($\theta_2 = 90°$).
**Total internal reflection**: all the light reflects. Needs bigger $n$ into smaller $n$, and $\theta_1 > \theta_c$.

where: critical angle (°), from $n_1$ into a smaller $n_2$

pts: **Prac**: turn a semicircular block until the ray skims ($\theta_c$). Turn more: all of it reflects.
**Optical fibre**: light stays in the **core** by total internal reflection. The **cladding** has a smaller $n$. Data travels far with little loss.
A ray that meets the wall at less than $\theta_c$ leaks out.
**Rainbow**: in each raindrop, sunlight refracts in, reflects off the back and refracts out, split into colours. Sun behind you.
Secondary rainbow: two reflections in each drop. Fainter, colours reversed.
**Mirage**: hot air near a road has a smaller $n$. Light from the sky bends back up into your eye, so the road looks wet. Over a cold sea, a boat can seem to float in the sky.
